title: Probabilistic spillover policy with cost-aware variant demotion and regional affinity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated pools occasionally hit transient saturation (e.g., bursty tenant traffic, pod reboots). Current deterministic overflow rules send traffic to hosted immediately when a hard capacity threshold is crossed, which causes rapid oscillation and billing surprises for customers. We need a more graceful, tenant-aware mechanism that: 1) preserves tenant affinity to their dedicated region/tier when possible, 2) limits cost exposure by demoting to lower-cost model variants before moving to hosted, and 3) prevents noisy oscillations with probabilistic damping and short-term prioritization decay.

Goal: Implement a probabilistic spillover policy that computes per-tenant spill probability based on short-term capacity pressure, tenant priority (reservation), and recent latency/error signals. Before routing to hosted, attempt cost-aware variant demotion (e.g., q4_0 -> q3_0 or lower-precision kernels) for a fraction of requests. Provide clear circuit breakers and observability so customers and SREs can understand decisions and opt into stricter or more lenient behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Default policy routes no more than 10% of steady-state requests to hosted for tenants with dedicated capacity under simulated 150% burst load
When capacity pressure is moderate (75-100%), 60-80% of overflow is handled via variant demotion instead of hosted spillover in canary experiments
No more than 1.5x increase in 95th percentile latency for demoted variants under synthetic workloads compared to baseline dedicated variant
Dashboard exposes per-tenant spill probability, recent demotion rate, and hosted spill counts; alerts fire when hosted spill exceeds SLA thresholds
Runbook updated with concrete steps to force-stop probabilistic spillover and to revert demotion rules within 5 minutes
implementation_plan: Design new routing decision function in orchestrator: inputs = (tenant_id, region, tier, pool_capacity_utilization, short_term_error_rate, tenant_priority, token_budget_remaining)
Compute a spill_score (0..1) combining capacity_utilization (weighted), priority decay, and recent error trend; convert to spill_probability with configurable hysteresis and smoothing

Introduce a demotion engine that selects compatible lower-cost model variants that maintain token compatibility and fallback to hosted only after demotion attempt fails or probability condition triggers hosted route
Add tenant-level policy knobs: max_hosted_spill_rate, demotion_allowed (true/false), priority_weight, emergency_cutover (force-hosted)
Update routing metadata to annotate traces with decision_reason and variant_path to improve observability
Backend changes: modify capacity-proxy to return short-term utilization histograms; extend routing cache to store per-tenant decay windows
Frontend/Console: new per-tenant toggles and a visualization for spill probability over time
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Ship policy off-by-default behind feature flag; enable for internal tenants only (redwood-infra, demo accounts) for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (Small Beta): Enable for 5 low-risk external tenants with explicit opt-in; collect telemetry for 1 week
Phase 3 (Gradual Ramp): Enable default policy for new dedicated customers with soft limits; gradually raise global canary percentage to 50% over 3 weeks
Phase 4 (Full): Enable globally with a 4-hour emergency kill switch available in Console and API
Rollback: immediate kill switch drains probabilistic path and forces deterministic fallback to previous overflow behavior; priority_retention flag prevents demotion if enabled by tenant
telemetry_and_alerts: Metric: per-tenant.hosted_spill_count (rate) - alert if sustained > configured SLA for 5 minutes
Metric: per-tenant.demotion_ratio (hosted_spill_count / total_overflows) - monitor and set warning when < 0.5 during moderate pressure
Metric: per-tenant.spill_probability - expose histogram and sample traces for values > 0.2
SLOs: ensure 99th token success rate remains within historical baseline; create regression alert tied to evaluation prompts
Tracing: annotate decision_reason and variant_candidate in distributed traces for post-incident analysis
test_plan: Unit tests for spill_probability computation across edge cases (zero capacity, full capacity, negative error trends)
Integration tests: synthetic traffic generator that simulates tenant bursts across regions and verifies demotion vs hosted outcomes under configurable weights
Performance test: confirm demotion engine does not add >3ms p95 decision latency to routing path
Chaos test: simulate pool reboots and ensure probabilistic damping prevents oscillation (assert hosted_spill_rate remains bounded)
E2E regression: run existing eval prompt set to ensure model-quality regressions from demotion are within acceptable thresholds
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Demoted variants cause quality regressions for critical customers -> Mitigation: tenant opt-out and strict per-tenant QA evaluation sets before enabling demotion
Risk: Probabilistic spillover is hard to reason about for customers -> Mitigation: expose deterministic controls (max_hosted_spill_rate) and a real-time visualization in Console
Risk: Billing surprises if too much traffic goes to hosted during long bursts -> Mitigation: conservative default weights, tenant-level alerts, and billing cap that triggers emergency_cutover
Risk: Increased complexity in routing logic makes debugging harder -> Mitigation: decision_reason attached to every routed request and sampling traces to Sentry/Jaeger
